# Veilguard
> A security checkup for apps built with AI. Paste your app's link and get a plain-English security grade in about a minute — plus the exact fix for every issue.

## What is Veilguard?
Veilguard is a self-serve website that checks whether an app built with AI coding tools is safe. You paste your live app's URL and, in about 60 seconds, get an A-to-F security grade and a prioritized list of every issue — each explained in plain English with the exact fix. No install, no editor plugin, no command line. For a deeper look you can optionally connect GitHub or Supabase with read-only access. After the first scan, monitoring keeps re-checking your app on every deploy.

## Who it is for
Founders and builders who shipped a real, working app with an AI tool (Lovable, Bolt, Replit, v0, Cursor) and are now charging customers or growing — usually without a security team, and often without the ability to read their own code. The core question Veilguard answers: "I built this fast and it's making money, but is it actually safe?"

## The problem it solves
AI coding tools let anyone ship a working app in a weekend, but they're built to make apps work, not to make them safe — and they never say what they left open. Nearly half of AI-generated code contains a security vulnerability. So people launch apps that take payments and store customer data with serious holes they can't see: exposed API keys, databases anyone can read, and logins with no real lock on the door.

## How it works (six steps)
1. Scan — paste your live app's URL; Veilguard checks it from the outside the way an attacker would (optionally connect GitHub or Supabase read-only for a deeper look).
2. Grade — in about 60 seconds you get an overall A-to-F grade and a prioritized list, worst issues first.
3. Understand — each issue is explained in plain English: what it is, what it means for you, and how serious it is.
4. Fix — for every issue Veilguard gives the exact fix: ready-to-paste code/SQL, or a copy-and-paste prompt you hand to your AI tool to apply.
5. Confirm — re-scan and watch the issue turn green.
6. Stay safe — turn on monitoring and Veilguard re-checks on every deploy, emailing you the moment a new change opens a new hole.

## What it checks
Exposed secrets and API keys; database access rules (Supabase row-level security and Firebase rules — the most common and most damaging issue); logins and authentication; payment webhook verification; overly open CORS; injection attacks such as SQL injection; vulnerable or malicious dependencies; HTTPS and security headers; and secrets buried in git history.

## What makes it different
- It fixes, it doesn't just flag: most scanners hand you a scary list; Veilguard hands you the solution.
- Built for founders, not engineers: plain English throughout.
- Deepest where it matters: especially the Lovable + Supabase combination, where the worst issues cluster.
- Always on: a single scan is a snapshot; monitoring keeps watching as the app changes.

## Pricing
- Free scan ($0): full A-to-F grade and every issue found and explained. No signup.
- Guard ($19/month): unlimited scans, all fixes, auto re-scan on every deploy, instant alerts, and a deep Supabase & Firebase audit. This is the core product.
- Fix Pack ($19 one-time): all fixes for one scan, including copy-paste code and AI prompts, plus a downloadable PDF report.

## Privacy
The free scan only looks at what is already public — what an attacker can see anyway. Deeper checks are opt-in, read-only, and your source is never stored; you control access and can revoke it.

## Honest scope
Veilguard catches the common, high-impact mistakes behind almost every vibe-coded breach — a strong first line of defense and safety net. For a high-risk or regulated product it is a foundation to pair with a professional audit, not a replacement for one.
